# SVG tools (local dev only)

Use this when a task involves SVG: editing, animating, optimizing, converting or rasterizing. These tools are for **local development only**: never add them to the deployed site (`docs/`), to CI or GitHub Actions, or to `requirements.txt`.

## How to choose

1. Pick the highest-ranked tool below that fits the job (same category or the same task). Rank already combines the editorial weight with how much each tool has actually been used.
2. Tools with a base weight under 2 are kept as warnings (stale, deprecated, unverified or not SVG tools). Do not start new work with them.
3. Read the tool's caveats first (`tools/svg-tools/RECOMMENDATIONS.md`, or below for the top 8). Tools marked UNVERIFIED or secondary have facts that need re-checking, prices especially. Do not state a price as fact without re-checking it.
4. After you actually use a tool, log it so the ranking learns:

```bash
python3 tools/svg-tools/scripts/svgtools.py use <id>            # add --times N for several uses
python3 tools/svg-tools/scripts/svgtools.py list --top 10       # current ranking (as of today)
```

Only change weights (`svgtools.py weight <id> <0-10>`) when the user asks. Do not edit `tools.json` by hand; use the CLI, then `svgtools.py render`.

- **Boxy SVG** (`boxy-svg`): Facts are secondary-source and prices conflict across sources; re-check on boxy-svg.com before buying.
- **Figma** (`figma`): Facts are secondary-source and prices disagree between sources; re-check on figma.com before relying on them.
- **LottieFiles (platform + Lottie Creator)** (`lottiefiles`): Facts are secondary-source and prices disagree between sources; re-check on lottiefiles.com before relying on them.
- **Rive** (`rive`): Editor pricing is secondary-source and free-tier limits are quoted differently by third parties; re-check on rive.app.

## Caveats for the top 8

- **SVGO** (`svgo`): Default preset can strip viewBox-less sizing, ids or title/desc that your CSS/JS/animation relies on; disable cleanupIds/removeViewBox-type plugins when animating by id or CSS class. Current npm version 4.1.0.
- **ImageMagick** (`imagemagick`): Security: ImageMagick has a long CVE history in SVG/MVG/MSL and URL/delegate handling. Never feed it untrusted SVG without a restrictive policy.xml (disable MVG/MSL/URL/HTTPS coders, limit resources). Distro default policy files are 'open' and meant for trusted/sandboxed use. For local dev with your own files this is fine. A policy can block SVG outright (users hit 'not authorized' errors). If you only need SVG -> PNG, resvg or rsvg-convert are more predictable. Current release number NOT verified (a Cygwin announcement from Dec 2025 lists 7.1.2.3).
- **Inkscape** (`inkscape`): Latest stable tag found on GitLab: INKSCAPE_1_4_4 (2026-05-05); master is 1.5-dev. Inkscape-specific metadata bloats files, so run SVGO or save as Plain SVG before committing.
- **Figma** (`figma`): Free Starter plan exists ($0, limited files per team folder; AI credits cap figures differ by source). Dev Mode needs a paid Dev/Full seat. Exact current prices vary between third-party sources and could not be checked on figma.com (host blocked in this session). Known SVG export quirks (secondary sources): layer-name-derived ids can contain unsafe characters; text outlining changes the file size and loses editability; effects such as blurs/blend modes/some gradients may not round-trip. Treat Figma export as a starting point and run it through SVGO. Not verified on the official help centre.
- **GSAP (GreenSock)** (`gsap`): README states that thanks to Webflow, GSAP is now free including the bonus plugins formerly Club-only (SplitText, MorphSVG, etc.), 'even for commercial use'. It is still source-available under a custom licence, not MIT: the Standard licence has restrictions (I could not read gsap.com/standard-license to confirm the exact limits; commonly cited one is no use in tools that compete with Webflow's visual animation tooling). Read it before shipping, though the user said local dev only.
- **LottieFiles (platform + Lottie Creator)** (`lottiefiles`): Official LottieFiles help centre says Lottie Creator is free but free users can export only 5 animations; paid plans unlock more exports plus optimisation and extra formats. Docs say free workspaces in the Figma plugin are capped at 5 saved files and 20 MB. Third-party sources disagree on paid prices (roughly $20-$50 per user per month); lottiefiles.com was unreachable from this session so current prices not verified. Whether dotLottie export is available on the free tier is unclear. Lottie is not SVG: it is an animation format that can embed vector shapes; round-tripping back to SVG is not a thing.
- **anime.js** (`anime-js`): v4 changed the API from v3 (named imports like `import { animate } from 'animejs'`); old tutorials may break.
- **dotlottie-web (LottieFiles player)** (`dotlottie-web`): Version number is pre-1.0 on npm so expect API churn. Older @lottiefiles/lottie-player (MIT, v2.0.12) is the web component; its maintenance state was not checked.
